title: Sats Stacker — DCA vs lump sum, simulated
description: A dollar-cost-averaging versus lump-sum simulator running on a seeded, clearly fictional random-walk price series: set the buy amount, frequency, duration, volatility and trend, and both strategies are replayed on an animated chart of value against money invested. A side-by-side comparison shows sats stacked in whole satoshis, average cost, return, maximum drawdown, worst point versus cost basis and days underwater.
prompt: I've stacked sats for years and I want an honest visual answer to the DCA versus lump-sum question, without pretending to be real market data. Build a simulator on a seeded fictional price series (geometric Brownian motion is fine), labelled everywhere as a simulation and not financial advice. Let me choose the amount, frequency, duration and a volatility preset, show an animated chart of holdings versus cost basis, the sats accumulated, drawdown stats, and a side-by-side comparison of the two strategies. Deterministic with ?seed=, one HTML file, no network.

methodology: Independent oracles in the spec: DCA sats are recomputed as the sum of floor(amount / price × 100,000,000) over the exposed price series and buy days, and the lump sum as one floor at day one.
Maximum drawdown for both strategies is recomputed from the exposed value series and compared to 5 decimal places; the declared winner must match the final values.
Schedule arithmetic: weekly, 30-day and daily buy counts over 365 days (53, 13, 365) are checked through the invested totals.
Determinism: the same ?seed= reproduces the identical price series after reload; a new seed changes it.
Animation driven by page.clock (install, pauseAt, runFor) to catch a mid-animation frame and the finished state; other tests use reduced motion so results appear at once.
Responsive check at 360px caught control rows overflowing the viewport; the chart also switches to a narrower viewBox on small screens so its labels stay readable.
risks: Floating-point rounding in satoshi conversion (always floor, never round) drifting from the oracle.
Downsampled chart paths hiding the true extreme values, so the stats are computed on the full series, not the plotted one.
Users mistaking the simulation for real prices; the disclaimer is persistent and in the verdict context.
Long durations (8 years daily = 2,920 buys) slowing SVG rendering on phones.
qa.playwright: The page exposes read-only getters on window.__sats for prices, buy days and value series, which turned financial assertions into plain arithmetic in the spec rather than scraping formatted currency. Randomness is pinned with ?seed= and a mulberry32 generator feeding Box-Muller normals. The reveal animation is a requestAnimationFrame loop, so one test installs and pauses a fake clock and steps it with runFor to see a partly drawn chart and then the finished one, while every other test emulates reduced motion to skip it. Keyboard scrubbing (Home, End, arrows) gives a deterministic way to test the tooltip without pointer coordinates. Chart pixels are never asserted.
coverage: Whole-satoshi oracle for DCA and lump sum, invested totals and average cost
Buy schedules for weekly, 30-day and daily frequencies and duration changes
Drawdowns and winner recomputed in bear and bull trends
Clock-driven animation and keyboard scrubbing of the readout

a11y: Controls are native inputs, selects and toggle buttons with aria-pressed. The chart is focusable with a label explaining arrow-key scrubbing, the readout gives every value as text, and the verdict is an aria-live region so changes in settings are announced.
